scopeNote: Vessel populations, berth and marina infrastructure, new-registration flows, seasonality indicators and order-of-magnitude electronics-spend context for the recreational and small-professional marine market in Spain, Portugal and the Galicia / Northern Portugal focus area. It contains no EMBARCARTE measurement, no customer contact and no paid data.
retrievalSession: Single desk-research session on 2026-10-31. All sources in this file were accessed on that date (some only as the search-engine excerpt of the cited page, stated in limitations). No page was accessed on any other date by this workstream.

sources.title: El mercado náutico cierra 2025 con estabilidad y un último trimestre favorable (summary of ANEN 'Informe del Mercado de Embarcaciones de Recreo 2025', based on Dirección General de la Marina Mercante data)
sources.publisher: InfoPuertos (trade press, publishing the ANEN report)
sources.limitations: Trade-press summary of the ANEN report, not the ANEN PDF itself. The article states a 2025 total of 4,992 registrations while its own provincial table sums to 4,991 (one-unit rounding or omission), so both readings are recorded. 'Matriculación' is a new-registration event, not the size of the registered fleet.

sources.title: El mercado náutico español registra 5.027 embarcaciones de recreo en 2024, un 15,9% menos (ANEN annual report on DGMM data)
sources.limitations: Contemporaneous press summary of the ANEN 2024 balance (including personal watercraft). The 2024 figure printed here (5,027) differs by 11 units from the 2024 column of the later ANEN 2025 report table (5,038), which is consistent with a data revision; neither figure is presented as exact.

sources.title: El mercado náutico español cierra 2023 con 5.976 matriculaciones
sources.limitations: Only the search-result excerpt of this page was read, not the full article. Used solely to place the 2024 decline in a three-year sequence; the 2023 total is not independently re-derived here.

sources.title: DGRM reúne com entidades da Náutica de Recreio (news release on recreational craft registration procedures)
sources.publisher: Direção-Geral de Recursos Naturais, Segurança e Serviços Marítimos (DGRM), Portugal
sources.limitations: An official statement of national aggregates ('cerca de 85.000') with no table, no breakdown by region, length or activity, and no definition of what the registration count excludes. The wording is approximate and the release is a procedural news item, not a statistical yearbook.

sources.title: Galicia fomenta el turismo náutico con el 6º Simposio de Clubs Náuticos (quoting Turismo de Galicia on 73 nautical-sports ports, 10,500 berths and 2024 transit vessels)
sources.limitations: Press report of a political speech quoting Turismo de Galicia; the underlying regional dataset is not published with the article. Berth counts are stated aggregate capacity, not occupancy, and 'transit vessels' is not defined (likely port-of-call visits, not unique vessels or nights).

sources.title: O paraíso da náutica deportiva (Rías Baixas berth capacity)
sources.limitations: Tourism-promotion page from the provincial council, no publication date displayed and no breakdown by port. States 'more than 4,600 berths' and 'around twenty facilities' on the Pontevedra coast; the figure is marketing-facing aggregate capacity, not audited occupancy.

sources.title: El sector de amarres en puertos deportivos crece tras la pandemia y mantiene una evolución positiva en 2024, según DBK (citing DBK Informa sector study)
sources.limitations: Only the search-result excerpt was read. The 289 ports / 133,400 berths figure is a commercial sector study (DBK) relayed by press, dated 'hasta marzo' 2025 in the excerpt; the study itself is not public, and its counting method (public vs private concessions, moorings vs dry berths) is not stated.

sources.title: Os galegos compran menos embarcacións recreativas (ANEN 2024 balance by Galician province)
sources.limitations: Regional press reading of the same ANEN dataset. Its Galician 2024 total (280) and provincial split (A Coruña 139, Pontevedra 128, Lugo 10, Ourense 3) do not reconcile with the 2024 column of the ANEN 2025 table (A Coruña 231, Pontevedra 162, Lugo 22, Ourense 2 = 417), which suggests a different inclusion of personal watercraft or of rental registrations. The discrepancy is recorded as unresolved, not averaged.

sources.title: Os portos deportivos da Coruña, a lume de biqueira este verán: 'Ata houbo que enviar barcos a outros portos'
sources.limitations: Only the search-result excerpt was read. A single-summer local press report ('case o 90%' berth occupancy, waiting lists, one club with 354 berths); it is not a measured occupancy series and does not represent Galicia or Spain.

sources.title: La demanda de plazas de alquiler crece un 40% en el puerto Juan Carlos I (Sanxenxo)
sources.limitations: Only the search-result excerpt was read. A single marina (Sanxenxo, Rías Baixas) reporting August 100% occupancy with a waiting list and July around 50%; transit-berth demand, not annual berth occupancy, and not generalisable to the region.

sources.title: Lista dos portos de abrigo para a náutica de recreio (PDF)
sources.limitations: Official but dated 2019 and read only through the search-result excerpt: it confirms that Viana do Castelo, Póvoa de Varzim, Vila do Conde, Leixões and the Douro are listed shelter ports for recreational boating. It does not give berth counts and may not reflect 2026 concessions.

sources.title: Viana Marina — port of call page (berth capacity)
sources.limitations: National tourism portal page, undated, requested in a German print view. States about 500 berths for vessels up to 20 m once all facilities are complete and 307 berths currently in the two basins around the Eiffel bridge. Capacity when built, not occupancy.

sources.title: Marina da Póvoa — port of call page (berth capacity)
sources.limitations: National tourism portal page, undated. States 241 permanent moorings, maximum vessel length 18 m and 2.5 m draught. Capacity, not occupancy; the operator's own price and availability data are not included.

sources.title: Marinas e Portos — listing of Portuguese recreational harbours (Douro Marina and Marina Porto Atlântico/Leixões entries)
sources.limitations: Only the search-result excerpt of the listings page was read. It states 300 moorings for Douro Marina and 240 for Marina Porto Atlântico (Leixões). Some Portuguese marinas (e.g. Vila do Conde) have no berth count in the retrieved excerpt, so the northern-Portugal total used in the sizing model is a documented floor, not a complete inventory.

sources.title: Public consultation document on recreational boating (citing APICAN for the number of registered recreational craft in Portugal, May 2024)
sources.publisher: SILIAMB / Agência Portuguesa do Ambiente (public consultation file)
sources.limitations: Only the search-result excerpt was read. It attributes to APICAN (the Portuguese nautical industry and trade association) a figure of 73,765 registered recreational craft in May 2024, which does not reconcile with the DGRM's 'about 85,000' in June 2024. Neither definition is published, so the gap is recorded as unreconciled rather than resolved.

sources.title: Marine Electronics Market Size & Share Report (market size estimates)
sources.limitations: Only the search-result excerpt was read; the full report is paid. Figures are a commercial research vendor's modelled estimate (global market estimated at USD 7,023.1 million in 2025 and USD 7,430.5 million in 2026), not an official statistic. The excerpt does not give the recreational-boat share, nor Spain or Portugal values, so it cannot be used to size the local market.

sources.title: OSPAR document on recreational boating pressures (restating ICOMIA Recreational Boating Industry Statistics 2017)
sources.limitations: Only the search-result excerpt was read. It reports 'approximately 6-6.5 million recreational vessels in European waters' on the authority of ICOMIA (2017); the underlying ICOMIA table, its country coverage and its definition of a vessel were not verified in this session. The data are nine years old at the retrieval date.

sources.title: ANEN news index page (item on Balearic registrations and charter share)
sources.limitations: Only the search-result excerpt of a tag-index page was read; it says that of the 904 vessels registered in the Balearics in 2024, 59% were charter-market registrations. The underlying article and dataset were not opened, so this is used only as a comparator signal, not as a measured charter share.

sources.title: Navega, s. coop. galega — naval electronics services (cooperative directory entry)
sources.limitations: A directory listing in which a Galician cooperative advertises on-board electronics installation, preventive maintenance and equipment repair. It proves that at least one such provider exists; it says nothing about how many providers exist, their capacity, their prices or their willingness to distribute MAREA.

sources.title: Cadenote Yacht, S.L. — Galician nautical company (repair yard, rigging and engine workshop, chandlery)
sources.limitations: A port business-directory entry describing one Galician company with a repair and maintenance workshop plus a physical and online chandlery. It evidences the existence of a refit/chandlery channel on the A Coruña coast but not its size, sales or procurement policy.

claims.claimText: Spain registered 4,992 new recreational craft in 2025, including personal watercraft, a fall of 0.9% on 2024.
claims.limitations: New registrations only, not the size of the registered fleet. The same source's provincial table sums to 4,991.

claims.claimText: Spain registered 5,027 new recreational craft in 2024, including personal watercraft, 15.9% fewer than in 2023.
claims.limitations: A later ANEN table prints 5,038 for the same year, so the 2024 baseline is subject to revision.

claims.claimText: Spain registered 5,976 new recreational craft in 2023.
claims.limitations: Excerpt-only reading. Establishes the direction and rough size of the 2023-2025 contraction, not an audited series.

claims.claimText: In 2025 Spanish new registrations were dominated by craft of up to 6 m: 3,492 units (70% of the total); 6-8 m accounted for 898 units (18%), 8-12 m 407, 12-16 m 144 and over 16 m 51.
claims.limitations: Length bands are the source's categories; the 51 units above 16 m are 1.0% of the market, and this flow says nothing about the existing fleet's length distribution.

claims.claimText: In 2025 Spanish new registrations by type were led by motor boats (2,066 units, 41.4%) and personal watercraft (1,394 units, 27.9%), with folding inflatable boats at 664 units (13.3%) and growing 47.2%.
claims.limitations: The three types named do not cover the whole market; sailboats and other types are not separately quantified in the retrieved article, so the shares must not be summed to 100%.

claims.claimText: Spanish rental/charter registrations were 1,418 in 2025, down 19.3% on 2024, after several years of strong growth.
claims.limitations: Rental registrations are a subset of the national total and are counted as registrations, not as active charter businesses.

claims.claimText: Spanish rental/charter registrations were 1,742 in 2024 (down 15.3%), with personal watercraft at 42% and motor boats at 35% of that rental market.
claims.limitations: The rental mix confirms that a large part of the charter fleet is not the kind of vessel that buys navigation electronics.

claims.claimText: In 2024, 70.3% of Spanish new recreational registrations were craft of up to 6 m and only 1.1% exceeded 16 m; motor boats were 42.5% and personal watercraft 31%.
claims.limitations: Consistent in direction with the 2025 table, which is the source actually used for computations; the 2024 shares serve as a cross-check.

claims.claimText: 2025 Spanish new registrations by province included Baleares 664 (-18.8%), Barcelona 564 (-1.1%), Murcia 491 (+85.3%) and Alicante 414 (+19.3%); in Galicia, A Coruña registered 209 (-9.5%), Pontevedra 229 (+41.4%), Lugo 27 (+22.7%) and Ourense 1.
claims.observedValue: Baleares 664; Barcelona 564; Murcia 491; Alicante 414; A Coruña 209; Pontevedra 229; Lugo 27; Ourense 1
claims.limitations: Province of registration is not necessarily province of use or mooring. Pontevedra's +41.4% is a single-year change on a small base.

claims.claimText: Spain had 289 recreational ports with about 133,400 berths, 67% of them on the Mediterranean coast, with an average of 462 berths per port (sector study dated to March 2025).
claims.limitations: Excerpt-only reading of a commercial study. Berth capacity is not the number of boats (moorings can be transient or vacant) and excludes trailer-launched and dry-stored craft.

claims.claimText: Galicia has 73 nautical-sports ports with 10,500 berths (Turismo de Galicia figures quoted in July 2025).
claims.limitations: Press report of a speech; the regional dataset and its counting method are not published with the article, and no date is given for the berth count.

claims.claimText: Galicia recorded 6,321 vessels in transit in 2024 according to the regional tourism authority's figures.
claims.limitations: 'Transit' is undefined; it most plausibly counts visiting vessels or port calls, which cannot be read as a resident fleet count.

claims.claimText: The Pontevedra coast (Rías Baixas) offers more than 4,600 berths across around twenty clubs and sports ports.
claims.limitations: Tourism-promotion page with no publication date; aggregate capacity, not occupancy, and the 'around twenty facilities' is a rounded statement.

claims.claimText: Galicia closed 2024 with 280 recreational craft registrations, 18% below 2023 (341), spread as A Coruña 139, Pontevedra 128, Lugo 10 and Ourense 3.
claims.limitations: This regional total is irreconcilable with the 2024 provincial column of the ANEN 2025 table (which sums to 417 for the same four provinces). The likely cause is different treatment of personal watercraft and/or rental registrations, but the sources do not state it, so the two figures are kept side by side and not averaged.

claims.claimText: Portugal had about 85,000 registered recreational craft and more than 90,000 people holding a valid navigator licence, per the DGRM in June 2024.
claims.limitations: Official but approximate and undated as a statistic; no regional breakdown, no active-vessel filter, and 'registered' may include craft that never go to sea.

claims.claimText: A Portuguese public-consultation document attributes to APICAN a figure of 73,765 registered recreational craft in May 2024, about 11,000 fewer than the DGRM's 'about 85,000' in June 2024.
claims.limitations: Excerpt-only reading of a consultation document quoting an industry association. The two Portuguese counts differ by 13% and neither definition is published; this is recorded as an unresolved contradiction, not as a third estimate.

claims.claimText: Documented berth capacity in four northern Portuguese recreational harbours is 307 at Viana do Castelo Marina, 241 at Marina da Póvoa, 240 at Marina Porto Atlântico (Leixões) and 300 at Douro Marina.
claims.limitations: Undated tourism-portal pages; Viana do Castelo's figure is the current basin count against a planned ~500, and Vila do Conde has no berth count in the retrieved source, so the northern-Portugal total is a floor.

claims.claimText: The Portuguese DGRM's official list of shelter ports for recreational boating includes Viana do Castelo, Póvoa de Varzim, Vila do Conde, Leixões and the Douro.
claims.unit: named northern shelter ports in the 2019 DGRM list
claims.limitations: The list is dated 2019 (recorded as STALE) and was read only through its search excerpt; it establishes the existence of the facilities, not their current capacity or commercial status.

claims.claimText: A Coruña's sports ports operated at close to 90% berth occupancy in summer 2024, with waiting lists for crane and dry use.
claims.limitations: Local press, single summer, no method stated; a peak-season indicator that says nothing about winter occupancy or about Galicia as a whole.

claims.claimText: Sanxenxo's Puerto Juan Carlos I reported August 2024 fully booked with a waiting list and July at about 50% occupancy, with rental-berth demand up 40%.
claims.unit: August, July occupancy and demand change, 2024
claims.limitations: One marina, one season, excerpt-only reading. Illustrates the shape of seasonal peaks in Rías Baixas; not a regional statistic.

claims.claimText: A commercial research vendor estimates the global marine electronics market at USD 7,023.1 million in 2025, rising to USD 7,430.5 million in 2026.
claims.limitations: Vendor estimate behind a paid report; the excerpt does not disclose the recreational-boat share, the geography split or the methodology, so this figure cannot be transferred to Spain, Portugal or Galicia.

claims.claimText: An OSPAR document restating ICOMIA (2017) statistics reports approximately 6-6.5 million recreational vessels in European waters.
claims.unit: recreational vessels in Europe (2017 source data)
claims.limitations: Nine-year-old second-hand citation whose underlying table was not verified; used only as an order-of-magnitude European context, never as an input to the local model.

claims.claimText: Of the 904 vessels registered in the Balearics in 2024, 59% were charter-market registrations according to a trade-press item.
claims.limitations: Read from a tag-index excerpt; the underlying article was not opened. Used as a comparator signal that charter-heavy markets behave differently from Galicia, not as a measured share.

claims.claimText: At least one Galician cooperative advertises on-board marine electronics installation, preventive maintenance and equipment repair as commercial services.
claims.unit: documented provider of this service type
claims.limitations: A directory entry is existence evidence only: it does not measure the number of providers, their capacity, or their interest in a new brand.

claims.claimText: At least one Galician nautical company operates a repair and maintenance workshop (sails, rigging, engines) together with a physical and online chandlery.
claims.limitations: Directory description of one company; it does not establish the size of the refit/chandlery channel, its stock policy or its supplier relationships.

claims.claimText: Viana do Castelo Marina will hold about 500 berths when all facilities are complete and currently offers 307 berths in two basins.
claims.limitations: The retrieved page is an undated tourism portal description; the completion date of the full plan is not stated, so the planned capacity is not usable as current supply.

claims.claimText: Of the 4,992 Spanish new registrations in 2025, exactly 1,500 units were 6 m or longer (6-8 m 898, 8-12 m 407, 12-16 m 144, over 16 m 51).
claims.unit: registrations of craft 6 m and above, 2025
claims.limitations: Simple sum of the four published bands; it inherits every limitation of the underlying registration data and describes a flow, not the installed base.

claims.claimText: Rental registrations represented 28.4% of all Spanish recreational registrations in 2025 (1,418 of 4,992).
claims.limitations: Derived from two figures in the same article; if the rental and total series use different inclusion rules the ratio is approximate.

claims.claimText: The three coastal Galician provinces accounted for 465 of the 4,992 Spanish new registrations in 2025, about 9.3%.
claims.limitations: Sum and ratio of published provincial figures (A Coruña 209 + Pontevedra 229 + Lugo 27); Ourense's single registration is excluded as non-coastal.

claims.claimText: The four Cantabrian-coast comparator provinces (Asturias, Cantabria, Guipúzcoa, Vizcaya) registered 354 new craft in 2025, fewer than Galicia's 465.
claims.limitations: Sum of published provincial totals (Asturias 129 + Cantabria 138 + Guipúzcoa 34 + Vizcaya 53). Registration province does not prove use location.

unavailableFacts.fact: Size of the registered recreational fleet in Spain (stock of vessels, not annual registrations).
unavailableFacts.reason: Not retrieved. The Dirección General de la Marina Mercante's registry publication (Lista Oficial de Buques) exists but is a large PDF series that was not parsed in this session, and no secondary source with a verifiable table was found.
unavailableFacts.missingEvidence: DGMM Lista Oficial de Buques / registro de buques de recreo table, or an ANEN publication with the fleet count and its definition.
unavailableFacts.nextAction: MC-10 or a follow-up desk task must obtain the registry table before any installed-base figure for Spain is used.

unavailableFacts.fact: Breakdown of the Portuguese recreational fleet by region (North, Centre, Lisbon, Algarve).
unavailableFacts.reason: The DGRM statement gives only a national approximate total; no regional table was found.
unavailableFacts.missingEvidence: DGRM statistical yearbook or registry extract by capitania/region.
unavailableFacts.nextAction: Request DGRM statistics or use the Portuguese national total only as an upper bound.

unavailableFacts.fact: Number of recreational craft registered or moored in Galicia and in Northern Portugal.
unavailableFacts.reason: Galicia's registered fleet count is not published in the sources retrieved; for Northern Portugal only marina berth capacity was documented.
unavailableFacts.missingEvidence: Xunta/Portos de Galicia fleet register, Portuguese registry by region.
unavailableFacts.nextAction: Treat berth capacity as a documented proxy in the sizing model and label the result as a proxy, not a fleet count.

unavailableFacts.fact: Age distribution of the recreational fleet in Spain, Portugal or Galicia.
unavailableFacts.reason: No retrieved source publishes vessel-age cohorts for recreational craft.
unavailableFacts.missingEvidence: Registry year-of-build distribution or ICOMIA age data by country.
unavailableFacts.nextAction: The refit thesis cannot be quantified in MC-09; treat 'old fleet means refit demand' as a hypothesis to test in MC-10.

unavailableFacts.fact: Annual marine-electronics spend per recreational vessel in Spain, Portugal or Galicia.
unavailableFacts.reason: No official or independent series was found; industry association totals for the equipment/accessories segment were not retrieved.
unavailableFacts.missingEvidence: ANEN industry turnover for equipment/accessories, or a distributor/installer sales sample.
unavailableFacts.nextAction: Keep per-vessel spend as an explicit ASSUMED scenario band in the sizing model and replace it only with measured data.

unavailableFacts.fact: Number and installed capacity of marine-electronics installers, yards and chandleries in Galicia and Northern Portugal.
unavailableFacts.reason: Only two individual provider pages were found (SRC-MKT-019, SRC-MKT-020); no register or association list was identified in this session.
unavailableFacts.missingEvidence: Regional installer/yard association member lists, Aclunaga or equivalent directories.
unavailableFacts.nextAction: Channel workstream or MC-10 must map providers before any installer-capacity assumption is treated as fact.

unavailableFacts.fact: Charter and rental fleet size in Galicia by province.
unavailableFacts.reason: SRC-MKT-008 explicitly states that no disaggregated rental-registration data exist for Galicia in the ANEN dataset it reports.
unavailableFacts.missingEvidence: Regional charter-licence register or Xunta tourism registry.
unavailableFacts.nextAction: Use national rental shares only as a comparator; do not attribute them to Galicia.

unavailableFacts.fact: Total recreational berth capacity in Portugal.
unavailableFacts.reason: Only four northern marinas could be documented; no national berth inventory was retrieved.
unavailableFacts.missingEvidence: APICAN / DGRM national marina and berth inventory.
unavailableFacts.nextAction: The Northern Portugal base used in the model must remain a documented floor.
